items.body:
The original fix is by @ywang96, with a follow-up refinement by @ivanium

## Summary

`truncate_computed_blocks()` asserts that every KV cache group holds at least
`num_computed_tokens // block_size` blocks. For a hybrid (full-attention + Mamba) model
served with a KV connector, a Mamba group can legitimately hold fewer: its blocks are whole
recurrent state, not per-token KV, and an external hit can supply the state at a boundary the
local group no longer covers. The assert turns that benign divergence into an engine-fatal
`AssertionError`, killing the prefill workers mid-run.

Fix: keep both asserts for groups that must cover the endpoint, and clamp only `MambaSpec`
groups.

```python
assert num_computed_tokens % manager.block_size == 0
num_blocks = num_computed_tokens // manager.block_size
if isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec):
    num_blocks = min(num_blocks, len(group_blocks))
else:
    assert num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)
```

A blanket `min()` over all groups would also stop the crash, but would silently mask a short
attention group — a real bug if it ever happens. Scoping to `MambaSpec` keeps that loud.

## Root cause

`truncate_computed_blocks()` has one caller, `Scheduler.schedule()`:

```python
if partial_tail and ext_tokens > partial_tail:
    new_computed_blocks = self.kv_cache_manager.truncate_computed_blocks(
        new_computed_blocks, block_aligned_local
    )
```

Both conditions must hold, which is why this is not hit by ordinary prefix caching:

- `partial_tail != 0` — the local hit ends on a prefix-match boundary that is not a block
  boundary. Requires `--prefix-match-unit` finer than the KV block size. For Kimi-K3 the
  platform raises the attention block to 1536 so the attention page covers the Mamba page,
  and `--prefix-match-unit 128` then makes a non-zero tail the common case.
- `ext_tokens > partial_tail` — the connector must hold *more* of the prefix than the local
  cache retains. `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` reports tokens beyond `block_aligned_local`,
  so when store and local cache hold the same prefix length the two are equal and the
  harmless `elif partial_tail:` branch runs instead. Divergence needs local eviction while
  the external store retains.

Both are satisfied by long chunked prefills: the request re-enters scheduling per chunk and
re-runs the lookup against its own earlier chunks, while concurrent requests churn the GPU
pool that the external store outlives.

Introduced in #49502, which added both the function and its caller. Still present on `main`.

## Reproduction

A PD deployment on 6 nodes (prefill 2 x TP8, decode 4 x TP1 -> DP16/EP16), MultiConnector
with NIXL plus MooncakeStore, `--enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128`, attention
block 1536, 800 GB store against a 1,980,479-token GPU pool.

16 requests of 98,944 prompt tokens each (`64 * 1536 + 640`, so the tail is
128-aligned and not 1536-aligned), raw token-id prompts, concurrency 8. Prefill died 7
requests in:

```
vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:797   in schedule
    self.kv_cache_manager.truncate_computed_blocks(
vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:792 in truncate_computed_blocks
    assert num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)
AssertionError
```

All 7 requests that reached prefill logged external loads. The store was at 78% with zero
`insufficient space` warnings, so capacity pressure is not involved.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script (bash + curl, no deps)</summary>

Two passes: the first populates the connector, the second replays the same prompts against
it. A single pass on a cold store writes but never reads (`Get=0`) and cannot reach the
guarded branch, so it would pass misleadingly — the script reads
`vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` and reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS when no
external hit occurred. Prompts are raw token-id lists so prefix lengths are exact.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: ./repro_truncate_assert.sh <router_port> [num_prompts] [prompt_tokens]
#   METRICS_URL=http://<prefill-host>:<port>/metrics  # recommended; else INCONCLUSIVE
# Exit: 0 fix verified, 1 reproduced (non-200), 2 inconclusive (no external reads).
set -uo pipefail

PORT=${1:?usage: repro_truncate_assert.sh <router_port> [num_prompts] [prompt_tokens]}
NPROMPTS=${2:-16}
BLOCK=${BLOCK:-1536}          # attention block size the platform picks for the hybrid model
LEN=${3:-$((64 * BLOCK + 640))}   # 640 = multiple of the 128 match unit, not of 1536
CONC=${CONC:-8}
MAXTOK=${MAXTOK:-4}
URL="http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/v1/completions"
MODEL=${MODEL:-moonshotai/Kimi-K3}

WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# x stays below 2^31 so x*1103515245 fits a 64-bit signed int exactly.
gen_tokens() {
  local seed=$1 n=$2 x i; local -a a
  x=$((seed * 7919 + 13))
  for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
    x=$(((x * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7FFFFFFF))
    a[i]=$((1000 + x % 90000))
  done
  local IFS=,; printf '%s' "${a[*]}"
}

ext_hits() {
  [ -n "${METRICS_URL:-}" ] || return 0
  curl -fsS --max-time 5 "$METRICS_URL" 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '/^vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total/{print $2; exit}'
}

send() {
  local i=$1 t0 code dt
  t0=$(date +%s)
  code=$(curl -sS -o "$WORK/resp_$i.json" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 1800 \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              --data-binary "@$WORK/body_$i.json" "$URL" 2>"$WORK/err_$i")
  dt=$(($(date +%s) - t0))
  printf 'req %3d  HTTP %s  %4ds' "$i" "$code" "$dt"
  [ "$code" != 200 ] && printf '   <<< FAILURE  %s' \
    "$(head -c 200 "$WORK/resp_$i.json" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\n')"
  printf '\n'
}
export -f send; export WORK URL

echo "prompts: $NPROMPTS x $LEN tokens, concurrency $CONC, tail mod $BLOCK = $((LEN % BLOCK))"
[ $((LEN % BLOCK)) -eq 0 ] && { echo "!! block-aligned: partial_tail would be 0" >&2; exit 2; }

for ((i = 0; i < NPROMPTS; i++)); do
  { printf '{"model":"%s","prompt":[' "$MODEL"; gen_tokens "$i" "$LEN"
    printf '],"max_tokens":%d,"temperature":0}' "$MAXTOK"; } > "$WORK/body_$i.json"
done

fails=0; declare -A delta
for pass in 1 2; do
  echo; echo "--- pass $pass ---"
  before=$(ext_hits)
  seq 0 $((NPROMPTS - 1)) | xargs -P "$CONC" -I{} bash -c 'send {}' | tee "$WORK/p$pass.txt"
  after=$(ext_hits)
  n=$(grep -c FAILURE "$WORK/p$pass.txt" || true); fails=$((fails + n))
  [ -n "$before" ] && [ -n "$after" ] && \
    delta[$pass]=$(awk -v a="$before" -v b="$after" 'BEGIN{printf "%d", b-a}')
  echo "  external hits this pass: ${delta[$pass]:-unknown}   non-200: $n"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && break
done

echo
[ "$fails" -gt 0 ] && { echo "REPRODUCED -- $fails non-200; check prefill for the assert"; exit 1; }
[ -z "${METRICS_URL:-}" ] && { echo "INCONCLUSIVE -- no METRICS_URL, cannot prove the connector was read"; exit 2; }
[ "${delta[2]:-0}" -le 0 ] && { echo "INCONCLUSIVE -- pass 2 had no external hits; raise num_prompts"; exit 2; }
echo "PASS -- $((NPROMPTS * 2)) requests, 0 failures, pass 2 served ${delta[2]} tokens externally"
```

</details>

## Test

End-to-end, same recipe and workload, only the patched file differing:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| requests completed | 7 of 16, engine dead | 16 of 16, twice |
| `num_blocks <= len(group_blocks)` asserts | 1 | 0 |
| external loads logged | 28 (7 reqs x 4 ranks) | 64 (16 reqs x 4 ranks) |
| store reads | — | `Get: Req=256/256, Item=7168/7168` |
| connector clients | 8 -> 4 (ranks died) | 8, unchanged |

The second pass is the one that matters: a cold store is written but never read
(`Get=0`), so it cannot exercise the branch. Re-running against the warm store produced
external hits on all 16 requests — more store read traffic than the run that crashed —
with the engine intact.

Unit tests, run inside the built aarch64 image so `vllm._C` is present:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py   20 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k hybrid                       4 passed
```

The 4 cover both parameterizations of `test_hybrid_fa_deeper_hit_uses_external_mamba_state`
and of `test_hybrid_per_group_hit_divergence_with_connector`. They need network for
`ModelConfig("facebook/opt-125m")`; with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and that config uncached they
fail in pydantic validation before reaching any scheduler code.

Lint, using the revisions CI pins (`ruff==0.14.0` from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`;
`requirements/lint.txt` pins only `pre-commit` itself):

```
ruff check                 All checks passed
ruff format --check        3 files already formatted
mypy 2.3.0                 Success: no issues found in 1 source file
```

## Not a duplicate

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "truncate_computed_blocks"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "partial-tail hybrid prefix cache"
```

The first returns nothing: no open PR touches this function. The second returns adjacent
work, none of it this fix:

- #49502 (@Dao007forever) introduced both the function and its caller. **Merged**
  2026-07-27, not open.
- #50507 (@chaunceyjiang, open) extends partial-tail prefix reuse for hybrid models via the
  lookup and restore paths. It does not touch these asserts.
- #46453 (@howarlii, open) reports per-group hit divergence for hybrid + connector, but
  through `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group` convergence and different asserts
  (`num_new_tokens > 0`, `num_locally_computed_tokens <= ...`), and predates #49502.
- #50454 (@gdevenyi, open) is the same class of failure on the native offloading connector,
  asserting in `offloading/scheduler.py`, not through `truncate_computed_blocks`.
- #50630 (@mosafariuk, open) describes the adjacent design gap: no capability flag declares
  which KV kinds may be peeked past a candidate boundary, so each implementation excludes
  Mamba by hand.

No open PR or issue reports this assert.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change: the follow-up commit is co-authored with OpenAI
Codex, and the reproduction, e2e verification, and this description were produced with
Claude Code. A human author reviewed every changed line.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix DSD K-lookup to count sampling-only requests, preventing K thrashing at batch boundaries
items.body:
## Description

The dynamic speculative decoding (DSD) K-lookup in `scheduler.py` uses `len(num_scheduled_tokens)` to index into `dynamic_sd_lookup`. This counts **all** scheduled requests, including mid-prefill/chunked-prefill requests. When prefills are mixed with decodes, they temporarily inflate the batch size and cause K to thrash between values as requests enter and leave prefill — a contributing factor to the catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse reported in #49548.

### Example

With schedule `[[1, 2, 2], [3, 16, 0]]` (K=2 for batch ≤ 2, K=0 for batch ≥ 3):

| Step | Requests | Old count | Old K | New count | New K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 decode + 1 prefill (512 tok) | 3 | 3 | **0** | 2 (decode-only) | **2** |
| 2 decode + 1 prefill (1 tok chunk) | 3 | 3 | **0** | 2 (sampling-only) | **2** |

The old code flips K from 2→0 every time a prefill joins 2 decodes, then back to 2 when it leaves. Each flip changes the verify-token count, forward shape, and CUDA graph dispatch.

### Fix

Count only requests that will **sample this step** (decode or final-prefill-chunk that reaches sampling), using the same phase-transition predicate the scheduler uses elsewhere:

```python
req.num_computed_tokens + num_tokens >= req.num_tokens + req.num_output_placeholders
```

This correctly handles:
- Pure decode requests
- Mid-prefill chunked requests (excluded — will not sample)
- Final prefill chunks that reach sampling (included — will sample)
- 1-token prefill chunks that are NOT final (excluded)
- Spec-padded decode requests (impossible in DSD mode — spec padding is gated on `dynamic_sd_lookup is None`)

If no requests reach sampling (all mid-prefill), falls back to `len(num_scheduled_tokens)` to preserve original behavior.

## Benchmark

Dual RTX 5090, TP=2, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-FP8, MTP k=2, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` + #49652 to preserve FULL CUDA graphs.

| Scenario | Before (±stdev) | After (±stdev) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4-session × 256 tok | 195 ± 164 t/s | **190 ± 49 t/s** | Variance −70% |
| 8-session × 256 tok | 308 ± 67 t/s | **412 ± 163 t/s** | +34% mean |
| Single-stream 32k | 285 ± 3 t/s | **289 ± 1 t/s** | Unchanged |

The variance reduction confirms K thrashing is eliminated. The multi-session mean remains below no-spec baseline due to a separate issue (wasted drafter forward at K=0 — see #49548 H1 analysis).

## Complementary to #49652

This fix targets the scheduler-side K-selection pathology (#49548 H3). PR #49652 fixes the worker-side MRV2 CUDA graph capture crash (#48494). Both are needed for functional DSD with FULL CUDA graphs on MRV2.

## Test

- `py_compile vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — PASS
- `pytest test_dynamic_sd_sampling_only_k_lookup` — 1 passed (8/8 edge cases)
- Live runtime verified on dual RTX 5090 with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B FP8 + MTP + MRV2 + DSD

Note: vLLM native scheduler tests require full dev install (`pip install -e .`). The standalone test validates the core predicate logic.

Fixes part of #49548.

items.title: [Bugfix] Install the weight offloader in the V2 model runner
items.body:
Fixes #50672

`set_offloader(create_offloader(...))` is only called from the V1 GPU model runner.
The V2 runner never installs an offloader, so `make_layers()` gets the process-global
default `NoopOffloader` and `--cpu-offload-gb` is silently a no-op.
`KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration` is in `DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES`, and
`_is_default_v2_model_runner_model()` also returns True for any dense model, so this
hits Kimi K3 and most non-MoE models.

The fix mirrors the V1 wiring: create the offloader in `__init__` before the model is
built, and call `post_init()` at the end of `load_model()`. Nothing else was missing,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py` already calls `get_offloader().sync_prev_onload()`
and `join_after_forward()`.

The existing `test_cpu_offload` only compares outputs with and without offloading, and
not offloading produces identical outputs, so it passed vacuously on V2. Added
`test_cpu_offload_is_applied`, which asserts the offloader actually ran, parametrized
over both runners.

**Tested** on 8x A40 (sm_86), driver 560.35.03, built from source against CUDA 12.6 /
torch 2.13.0+cu129, TP=1:

- `test_cpu_offload_is_applied`: fails on `[1]` (V2, `NoopOffloader`) and passes on `[0]`
  (V1) without the patch; both pass with it.
- `tests/basic_correctness/test_cpu_offload.py::test_cpu_offload`: 4 passed. This now
  runs with real UVA offloading on V2, with and without CUDA graphs, and still matches
  the non-offloaded baseline.
- `tests/v1/streaming_input/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_streaming.py`: 2 passed.
- The patch also switches on the prefetch backend for V2, so I checked it by hand:
  `--offload-group-size 2 --offload-num-in-group 1` on V2 with CUDA graphs gives
  byte-identical greedy output to the baseline.
- `pre-commit run --files` on both touched files: all hooks pass, mypy included.

**Not verified:** Kimi K3 itself. It needs sm_90+ FP8 MegaMoE kernels and far more
memory than this box has, so the Kimi K3 part of the diagnosis is from reading
`vllm/config/vllm.py` and `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`, not from a run. Also untested here:
multi-GPU / TP / PP / EP, multimodal offload, `--cpu-offload-params`, and quantized
checkpoints (`tests/quantization/test_cpu_offload.py` needs FP8 or Marlin, which do
not run on sm_86).

The reporter's issue body was an empty template, so I could not reproduce their exact
run. I reproduced the defect its title describes. Thanks to @ee-redbull for filing it.

AI assistance was used to write this patch.

## Purpose
#48413 introduced two separate failures in the Multi-Modal Models (Extended Generation 3) TG. - [CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82790/list?sid=019fdad0-9b55-499d-9662-74da23816d75&tab=output)
The two types of failures are:
- NameError: name 'List' is not defined
- AttributeError: 'MiniCPMV' object has no attribute 'all_tied_weights_keys'

The second one has two parts; this PR addresses the second part of the second failure:
- The first issue, presented by the error message is circumvented by #49679, I didn't want to duplicate it in this PR.
Either #49679 should be merged before this, or this PR can absorb its change (or something similar). 
- After the AttributeError is fixed, a second issue presents itself: the tests are flaky. The flakiness is addressed by this PR.

The flakiness in the 6 minicpmv_26 presents itself in two different ways:
- (More common) - the hf reference produces all NaN outputs

items.title: [Bugfix] LoRA: normalize single-tensor lora_a in merged set_lora
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51409.

> **AI assistance disclosure** (per the [contributing guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing/)): this PR includes AI-generated code. The fix and the accompanying regression test were drafted with Claude Code; the reproduction, the before/after test runs, and the environment collection were carried out and reviewed under my direction. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

`MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA.set_lora()` declares `lora_a: torch.Tensor | list[torch.Tensor]` but only normalizes `lora_b`. A single 2-D `lora_a` of shape `[rank, input_size]` is passed through unexpanded, so `lora_a[i]` yields a 1-D **row** instead of the i-th slice's matrix, raising `IndexError` on any packed layer (fused QKV = 3 slices, gate_up = 2 slices):

| Combination | Function | Error |
|---|---|---|
| fused QKV, `fully_sharded_loras=True` | `MergedQKVParallelLinearWithShardedLoRA.slice_lora_a` | `too many indices for tensor of dimension 1` |
| gate_up, `fully_sharded_loras=True` | `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithShardedLoRA.slice_lora_a` | `too many indices for tensor of dimension 1` |
| fused QKV, `fully_sharded_loras=False` | `set_lora` copy loop | `tuple index out of range` |
| gate_up, `fully_sharded_loras=False` | `set_lora` copy loop | `tuple index out of range` |

A single tensor is a declared input, not caller misuse. Only a *fused* source produces one A — e.g. Megatron, which stores QKV as a single linear. Those weights reach `set_lora` when an RL trainer pushes them **in-memory** (`update_weights_from_ipc -> add_lora -> set_lora`), bypassing the loader that would otherwise assemble a per-slice list. In our case RL post-training (verl + vLLM + Megatron) with LoRA and TP>1 died on the first weight sync.

vLLM already treats `lora_a` as shared across slices: `expand_packed_lora()` does `expanded_a.append(a_i)` (*"replicate a_i for each"*), and `MergedColumnParallelLinearVariableSliceWithLoRA.set_lora()` in this same file already contains exactly this normalization under the comment *"Override to handle single tensor weights"*. Only the bare-tensor entry point on the base class was missed.

### Note on the count

The replication count is `len(lora_b)`, **not** `self.n_slices`. `expand_packed_lora()` zips `lora_a` against `lora_b`'s *groups*, so expanding to `n_slices` first would mis-pair A with B on layers like `in_proj_qkv` + `in_proj_z` — silently wrong weights rather than a crash.

### Scope

Adapters loaded **from disk** cannot reach this, and I verified that rather than assuming: `worker_manager._load_adapter()` builds `expected_lora_modules` by expanding packed modules into their constituents (`q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`), so a checkpoint targeting the fused name (`qkv_proj`) is rejected by `check_unexpected_modules()` with a clean `ValueError` before reaching `set_lora`. The in-memory weight-push path is the only route.

Distinct from #37019, which generalizes `slice_lora_a` to arbitrary N but does not touch the base class's `set_lora` — I checked its diff; this gap survives it.

## Test Plan

All runs on the official nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-aarch64` (vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9`, 4x GB300, driver 580.159.04). Full `collect_env` output is in #51409.

1. **Standalone repro at real TP=2.** Builds `QKVParallelLinear` / `MergedColumnParallelLinear` plus the LoRA wrapper and calls `set_lora(0, lora_a, lora_b)` with `lora_a` as one 2-D tensor. A 2x2x2 matrix: {fused QKV, gate_up} x {`fully_sharded_loras` True, False} x {single tensor, per-slice list}. Loads no model, runs no kernel.

   ```
   torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 repro.py
   ```

2. **`tests/lora/test_layers.py`**, before and after the fix, including the new regression test.

## Test Result

### Standalone repro, TP=2

Before — 4/4 single-tensor combinations fail, 4/4 per-slice-list controls pass:

```
vllm 0.26.1rc1.dev457+gc810e5ee9 tp=2
[FAIL] qkv     fully_sharded=True  lora_a=single-tensor  -> :639 slice_lora_a  too many indices for tensor of dimension 1
[FAIL] qkv     fully_sharded=False lora_a=single-tensor  -> :323 set_lora      tuple index out of range
[FAIL] gate_up fully_sharded=True  lora_a=single-tensor  -> :559 slice_lora_a  too many indices for tensor of dimension 1
[FAIL] gate_up fully_sharded=False lora_a=single-tensor  -> :323 set_lora      tuple index out of range
[PASS] qkv     fully_sharded=True  lora_a=list
[PASS] qkv     fully_sharded=False lora_a=list
[PASS] gate_up fully_sharded=True  lora_a=list
[PASS] gate_up fully_sharded=False lora_a=list
4 combination(s) failed
```

After — 8 pass, 0 fail.

### tests/lora/test_layers.py

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| failed | 9 | 1 |
| passed | 162 | 170 |
| skipped | 144 | 144 |

The delta is exactly the 8 parametrizations of the new test. No previously-passing test regresses.

The 1 remaining failure is `test_get_masked_input_and_mask`, which fails **identically before and after** — pre-existing on this nightly and unrelated to LoRA merging (it covers vocab-embedding masking). Reporting it rather than filtering it out.

Caveat on environment: `vllm-openai` is a runtime image, so the suite needed `pip install pytest ray tblib` added. That is not a stock CI environment. The `torchrun` repro requires none of those and is the primary evidence.

## Test coverage added

`test_column_parallel_packed_single_tensor_lora_a` covers {gate_up, fused QKV} x {`fully_sharded_loras` True, False}.

No existing test could catch this. `tests/lora/test_layers.py` is the only file in `tests/` with a direct `set_lora()` call, and its call sites miss the combination: `populate_loras()` exercises the merged classes but feeds them via `PackedLoRALayerWeights.pack()`, which always builds a **list** `lora_a`, while the one site that passes a bare tensor targets `MergedColumnParallelLinearVariableSliceWithLoRA` — the sibling class that already normalizes.

The two fully-sharded sites live behind `if self.tp_size > 1`, so the test forces that branch by setting `tp_size = 2` on the layer. That is the one deliberately artificial thing here, and it is commented as such: `tp_rank` stays 0 and the buffers are sized for tp=1, so both `slice_lora_a()` and `slice_lora_b()` select the full width and the assertions are unchanged. All 8 parametrizations fail before the fix and pass after.

items.title: [BugFix] Bind fault-tolerance DP ports before publishing them
items.body:
## Purpose

`--enable-fault-tolerance` recreates both the EngineCore DP group and each worker CPU DP group after a `retry`. The recovery path selected every replacement port with `get_open_port()`, released the probe socket, published only the number, and bound the real TCPStore later. The worker-port window also crossed the EngineCore-to-worker collective RPC. A concurrent process could take any selected port and make recovery fail with `DistNetworkError ... EADDRINUSE`.

This PR removes probe-then-bind from fault-tolerance recovery:

- Adds the RFC #51275 `bind_ephemeral()` primitive, which returns a still-listening socket and its actual port.
- Engine DP rank 0 binds and holds its new port, publishes the number through the old DP store, and hands the same socket to the replacement TCPStore.
- The replacement Engine DP store becomes the coordination path for worker groups. Each worker-DP rank 0 binds its own port, publishes it under an epoch/local-rank key, and hands the same socket to its replacement TCPStore.
- EngineCore no longer pre-allocates worker ports, so no socket or file descriptor has to cross a process boundary.

The port remains kernel-owned continuously from selection until TCPStore takes ownership.

## Relationship to existing work

- Implements the fault-tolerance recovery case tracked by RFC #51275.
- Complementary to #51018: that PR fixes initial world/DP-group startup; this PR fixes the groups recreated after an FT `retry` and does not depend on #51018.
- Complementary to #51033: that PR covers API-server and EngineCore handshake ZMQ endpoints, not FT TCPStore groups.
- Duplicate-work checks: open PR searches for `51275 in:body`, `fault tolerance port get_open_port`, and `fault tolerance DP group port` found no PR covering this recovery path. #46370 and #41438 are broader FT feature/redesign work and do not modify these call sites.

## Test design

- Module/I/O: `EngineCoreSentinel._reinit_dp_group()` publishes coordination metadata; `WorkerSentinel.retry()` consumes it and installs replacement CPU groups.
- Failure guarded: another listener taking a port between selection/publication and TCPStore bind.
- Cheapest sufficient level: CPU-only unit tests replace distributed group construction with an observer that tries to bind the advertised port immediately before accepting the socket. The competing bind must fail for both Engine and Worker handoffs.

## Test results

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_port_reinitialization.py -q` — **2 passed**.
- `pre-commit run --files <four changed files>` — **all hooks passed**, including Python 3.10 mypy.
- `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <four changed files>` — **passed**.
- Direct CPU smoke test creating and destroying a world-size-1 Gloo group with `bind_ephemeral()` + `listen_socket=` — **passed**.
- The hardware E2E FT file could not be collected in this worktree because the local environment lacks the CUDA flash-attention extension. No model output or accuracy behavior changes.

## AI Disclosure

OpenAI Codex was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and drafting this description. The human submitter must review every changed line and understand and defend the change end-to-end before requesting maintainer review.


## Reproduced nightly A/B (2026-08-07)

Actual run: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on h200-0 baseline (`sha256:40e504de…`) and h200-1 PR head (`sha256:928dde7d…`), with GPU visibility enabled. A deterministic squatter takes the engine DP TCPStore port immediately after the baseline `get_open_port()` probe returns.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| base `47228db84c` | `DistNetworkError … EADDRINUSE` at TCPStore listen |
| PR head `320bbbb6a` | succeeds: `bind_ephemeral()` keeps rank 0's listener open and `stateless_init_torch_distributed_process_group(..., listen_socket=...)` takes it over |

The harness invokes the production `EngineCoreSentinel._reinit_dp_group()` with a real one-rank Gloo TCPStore, not a mocked bind. Reproduce by running the nightly image with `--network host`, injecting a squatter after `get_open_port()` returns on the base, and using the same fake engine/DP store setup as `tests/v1/fault_tolerance/test_port_reinitialization.py`; the PR head must not call `get_open_port()` in this path and must complete the reinit.

## Fresh nightly A/B confirmation (2026-08-07)

Re-ran the production `_reinit_dp_group()` harness concurrently after the final commit `320bbbb6a9`: h200-0 mounted base `47228db84c`, and h200-1 mounted the PR head, into `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` while retaining the installed CUDA extensions. Both runs used `--gpus all --network host`.

```text
base: The server socket has failed to listen … code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE
head: FIXED fault-tolerance Engine DP reinit passed with a held socket
```

The squatter deterministically binds the exact port returned after the base probe releases it. The head no longer exposes that engine-DP gap: `bind_ephemeral()` retains the listener until `TCPStore(master_listen_fd=…)` takes ownership.

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Route non-divisor small-head MLA decode to Gluon on gfx950
items.body:
Fixes #51232.

Kimi-K3 has 96 MLA query heads; at TP8 each rank gets 12 local heads.
12 is not a divisor of 16, so `use_gluon_decode` returned `False` in
"auto" mode, routing single-token decode to the padded ASM persistent
path. That path pads 12 heads to 16 and asks AITER for a `{bf16, fp8,
gqa=16, qseqlen=1}` kernel, which does not exist on gfx950 — every
rank crashes with `cannot get heuristic kernel` before the server
starts.

The Gluon MLA decode kernel handles any head count natively (no
padding), so the fix is to prefer Gluon for ALL small-head counts on
gfx950 in "auto" mode, not just divisors of 16. On gfx942 (no Gluon
build) the ASM path is still used for all counts — no behavior change.

`VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm` still forces the padded ASM
path if needed.

### Changes

- `rocm_aiter_mla.py`: remove the `m % num_heads == 0` gate from the
  "auto" return in `use_gluon_decode`
- `test_rocm_aiter_mla_head_padding.py`: update 3 assertions so
  non-divisor counts (12, 6) assert `is on_gfx950` instead of `not`

## Purpose

`tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py::test_dbo_dp_ep_gsm8k[deepep_high_throughput]` fails in AMD CI
roughly every other run. It is not a noisy measurement:
the outcome is decided when the server starts and then holds for its life, either around 0.65 on
GSM8K or around 0.60, with nothing in between. A degraded server truncates part of its generations
after four to six tokens, as if those requests never saw the few-shot examples.

They never did. A request can be admitted on a prefix cache hit against blocks that another request
in the same batch is only computing now, since those blocks are hashed and handed out while that
other request is being scheduled. Run whole, the step issues every KV cache write before any
attention read and the hit holds. Microbatching runs the two halves one after the other, so when
the writer sits in the second half the readers in the first half attend over blocks that are still
zero. In this test the first step of every evaluation is exactly that batch: one request computing
the shared 5-shot preamble of 672 tokens next to requests holding a cache hit on it. Which half the
writer lands in is fixed by arrival order at startup, which is why the verdict is fixed too.

## The change

Refuse to microbatch a step in which one request reads blocks another request writes in that same
step, and run it whole instead, through the `allow_microbatching` hook that already exists.
Everything else keeps microbatching, and decode steps leave the check before touching a block
table. The condition is not specific to a backend or a vendor, so the check is not gated on either;
the same symptom is tracked on Blackwell in
[#29913](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29913), where the test is marked xfail. Vetoing
on one rank settles it for all, since ranks agree on microbatching collectively.

## Evidence

An audit in the KV cache update op, which runs before a half writes anything, recorded per half the
blocks it writes, the blocks it reads as computed context, how many of those are still empty right
then and how many change afterwards. In the deciding step the first half reads 42 blocks, the
preamble at a block size of 16, finds all 42 empty, and all 42 change later. How many of those 42
the second half is the one to write predicts the outcome over eight starts without exception: the
five starts where it owned all 42 are the five that failed, and the three where it owned fewer or
none are the three that passed.

## Test Plan

DP=2 with EP, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat`, GSM8K with 256 questions and 5 shots, exactly as
the test runs it. Because the outcome is decided per server start, everything is repeated across
restarts rather than within one server, counting answers shorter than 12 tokens alongside accuracy.

## Test Result

Unpatched on current main, of six server starts one fails outright at 0.570 with 22 truncated
answers and one scrapes past at 0.625 with 3, while the other four are clean.

With this change, `pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py -k high_throughput` passes 10 of 10 runs
and takes as long as it did unpatched. Across eight restarts no start comes back with a truncated
answer, where unpatched starts reach 22, and the audit reports no half left reading a block the
other half owns.

items.title: [Bugfix] Stop Kimi K3 end-of-turn marker leaking into streamed content
items.body:
FIX #51399

## Purpose

The model closes a Kimi K3 assistant turn with `<|close|>message<|sep|>` right before the end-of-message token (see the `_K3_MESSAGE_CLOSE` comment in `structural_tag_registry.py`). The non-streaming tool parser strips that marker in `_strip_response_content`, but the streaming content path `_extract_response_content` only stopped content emission at `tools open` and `response close`. A turn that ends without a `response close` marker therefore streamed the raw XTML marker to the client:

| Path | Content for `Hello<|close|>message<|sep|>` |
| --- | --- |
| `extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming) | `Hello` |
| `extract_tool_calls_streaming` before this PR | `Hello<|close|>message<|sep|>` |
| `extract_tool_calls_streaming` after this PR | `Hello` |

The fix treats a complete `<|close|>message<|sep|>` as a content stop the same way `response close` already is, and adds the marker to the partial-suffix hold-back so a marker split across deltas cannot leak either. Behavior for content that ends in a partial marker prefix at truncation matches how the existing `response_close` hold-back already behaves.

Level of fix: the unary strip set is `response_open`, `response_close`, `message_close`; after this change the streaming stop-and-hold set covers exactly that set, so the divergence class inside this parser is closed. The reasoning parser keeps its own already-correct copy of this logic; unifying the two into a shared helper would couple the reasoning and tool parsers and is out of scope for a bugfix.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Open Kimi K3 tool parser PRs #50627 and #50628 make tool-call argument streaming incremental (issue #50604). Neither touches `_extract_response_content` or the content marker logic (checked their diffs on 2026-08-07). No open issue or PR covers the content marker leak.

## Test Plan

New `tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py` with two behavior tests:

- `test_streaming_content_stops_at_message_close`: streaming equals non-streaming for a turn ending in `<|close|>message<|sep|>` without `response close`.
- `test_streaming_content_holds_split_message_close`: the marker never leaks when deltas split it at chunk sizes 1, 3, and 7.

```
python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_kimi_k3_named_tool_choice.py
```

## Test Result

Both new tests fail before the fix (`AssertionError: assert 'Hello<|close|>message<|sep|>' == 'Hello'`) and pass after it. The pre-existing `test_kimi_k3_named_tool_choice.py` still passes. A local parity harness (7 output shapes including full response wrapper, consumed prefix, single and double tool calls, unicode and empty-string arguments, object arguments, each split at chunk sizes 1/3/7/full) reports zero streaming vs non-streaming mismatches after the fix.

This change affects serving-layer string extraction only, no model forward path, so no model evaluation is attached; the parity harness against `extract_tool_calls` covers the output contract.

An independent adversarial verification pass (separate agent, fresh context) confirmed the bug on the unfixed tree with its own fuzzer (the marker leaks at all 27 split offsets before the fix, at none after), confirmed reachability (`vllm/parser/kimi_k3.py` lines 116-119 bypass the reasoning-parser stripping whenever a tool parser is configured), and measured the one behavior change: content ending in a partial `message_close` prefix at EOS is now held back up to 22 chars, the same class of hold the existing `response_close` guard has always applied at up to 23 chars.

## What was not tested

No end-to-end serving run with a real Kimi K3 model: verification is parser-level on a CPU box, so the claim that a real detokenizer delivers the marker as contiguous literal text rests on `adjust_request` forcing `skip_special_tokens=False` and `spaces_between_special_tokens=False`, not on a live run. Whitespace-tolerant marker variants (`<|close|> message <|sep|>`) still leak on both trees; that gap is pre-existing for `response_close` too, is documented in the parser as defense-in-depth made a no-op by `adjust_request`, and stays out of scope here.

## AI assistance disclosure

This bug was found and fixed with AI assistance (Claude). The submitting human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests locally.

items.title: [Bugfix] Do not select Model Runner V2 when weight offloading is enabled
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix the silent no-op of model weight CPU offloading (`--cpu-offload-gb`, prefetch offload) when the V2 GPU model runner is selected. Fixes #51396.

The offloader singleton defaults to `NoopOffloader` and only the V1 runner installs a real one (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:980`); the V2 runner never calls `set_offloader`, so `make_layers()` wraps layers with the noop and nothing is offloaded — no log line, no warning. For workloads that need offloading (model bigger than VRAM) the result is an OOM whose message suggests unrelated remedies. Several architectures now default to V2 (`DeepseekV2ForCausalLM`, `Qwen2MoeForCausalLM`, …), so plain `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat --cpu-offload-gb 12` hits this with no V2 flag involved.

This PR takes the conservative route: declare weight offloading unsupported by V2 in `_get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features()` (plus an `OffloadConfig.is_enabled()` helper mirroring `create_offloader`'s backend selection), so that:

- default model-runner selection **falls back to V1** (where offloading works), with the existing "Model Runner V2 does not yet support …" warning;
- forcing `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` (or configs that force V2: dspark, PCP, diffusion) **raises a clear error** instead of silently not offloading. For those forced-V2 configs offloading genuinely does not work today, so a loud error is strictly better than the current silent no-op followed by OOM.

Wiring the offloader into V2 (parity with V1) is the better end state — the V2 cudagraph utilities already call `get_offloader().sync_prev_onload()` hooks — but that deserves its own validated change; this PR stops the silent failure now. Happy to follow up with the V2 wiring (and can test it on SM120 hardware) if that direction is preferred.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_v2_model_runner_unsupported_with_weight_offloading` (UVA and prefetch variants; asserts no offload entry in the baseline feature list).
- `pytest tests/test_config.py -k "offload or v2_model_runner"`.
- GPU before/after on RTX 5090 (32 GB, SM120, driver 610.57.04): DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat BF16 (29.26 GiB checkpoint), `cpu_offload_gb=12`, `enforce_eager`, default runner selection.

## Test Result

- `22 passed` for `pytest tests/test_config.py -k "offload or v2_model_runner"`.
- Before (main `8d9b52f7c2`): `Using V2 Model Runner` → `Model loading took 29.35 GiB` → no "Total CPU offloaded parameters" line → OOM (does not fit).
- After (this PR, same command): `WARNING … Model Runner V2 does not yet support model weight CPU offloading (--cpu-offload-gb / prefetch offloading); using the V1 model runner instead.` → `Total CPU offloaded parameters: 12.13` → `Model loading took 17.21 GiB`.
- Control on an unmodified recent build (Qwen3.5-4B-FP8, `cpu_offload_gb=2`): V2 loads 5.35 GiB with no offload line; V1 loads 3.29 GiB with `Total CPU offloaded parameters: 2.01` — confirming the underlying no-op this PR guards against.

## Purpose

Fix long-prompt prefill failures in `FlashInferMLASparseSM120Impl`.

The SM120 sparse backend inherits `supports_dense_mha_prefill = True` from `MLAAttentionImpl`, but it implements only the sparse `forward_mqa` path. When a long prompt selects dense or masked MHA prefill, the shared MLA router accesses dense-path state such as `masked_mha_available`, which this implementation does not define.

## Purpose

Fixes #51313.

Kimi-K3 plain FP8 KV cache requires an FP8 prefill query, but query
quantization is currently limited to device capability 100 and compatible MLA
prefill backends. On Hopper or with an unsupported backend, the model previously
initialized successfully and then failed on the first prefill with an assertion
that recommended enabling `use_prefill_query_quantization`, even though that
setting could not be honored.

This change validates the combination during model initialization and points
users to `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, which uses a BF16 prefill query and is
the supported Hopper path.

open PR titles and bodies for #51313, Kimi-K3 Hopper FP8 prefill query
quantization, and the `fp8_ds_mla` workaround. No implementation for this issue
was found. Related PRs using `fp8_ds_mla` address different MLA backends or
performance paths.

- Reject Kimi-K3 `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3` cache configurations when FP8 prefill

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Prevent Inkling block-end leakage with tools

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
Fixes #51387.

## Problem

When tools are enabled, an Inkling plain-text response can leak `<|end_message|>` or `<|content_model_end_sampling|>` into `content`. This commonly occurs on the synthesis turn after a tool result, when the model answers without opening another tool block. Both streaming and non-streaming paths are affected.

## Root cause

The reasoning pass runs with tool parsing disabled and forwards tool syntax for the downstream tool pass. Inkling reuses its block-end tokens for reasoning, text, and tool blocks, so classifying them only by terminal identity forwards an ordinary text closer even when no tool region is open.

A semantic `TOOL_CALL_END` event is not a reliable lexical boundary for the shared engine. For example, MiniMax closes an inner `<invoke>` before closing the surrounding `<minimax:tool_call>` wrapper. Several other grammars also have wrapper closers with no transition from the reasoning pass's projected `CONTENT` state.

## Fix

- Track whether the reasoning pass is forwarding a lexical tool region.
- Derive tool-region exits structurally from tool-state → non-tool-state transitions.
- Apply shared block-end terminals normally outside a forwarded tool region.
- Forward complete tool syntax, including wrapper closers, while a tool region is open.
- Clear the forwarded span even when the projected skip state has no transition for the closer.
- Add served two-pass and shared-engine regression coverage for plain text, reasoning, multi-tool sequences, parser reuse, both Inkling end tokens, and transitionless closers.

The earlier generic cleaned-content fallback in `abstract_parser.py` is no longer part of this change; fixing marker ownership in the reasoning pass resolves #51387 without changing the no-tool-call contract for every engine-backed parser.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/parser/engine -q` — 3758 passed
- Ruff check on all changed Python files — passed
- Ruff format check on all changed Python files — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

No live model evaluation was run. This is a parser-only change with deterministic CPU-only coverage, and an Inkling model was not available locally.

## Scope and attribution

This does not duplicate #49876, which handles no-tools plain-text mode, or #50528, which handles tool-call handoff without a thinking block.

The structural implementation and regression tests were adapted from [Ben Browning's reviewed proposal](https://github.com/bbrowning/vllm/commit/7bfa88a9a6007d6277bc9ae9c2bc47739e18b400); co-author attribution is preserved in the commit trailers.
